purpose: Qualitative demand/friction intelligence for the single Stödassistenten learning system. Scores are prioritization signals, not measured search volumes and not proof of eligibility, insurance coverage or factual truth. Community discussion is discovery-only; material claims require current primary-source verification.

scoring.priority_rule: Prioritize combinations of high demand, high friction, high consequence and weak current product coverage. Scores are qualitative prioritization, not measured search volume.

natural_language_queries: jag driver eget utan anställda gäller TFA om jag skadar mig på jobbet
har jag Afa arbetsskadeförsäkring som egenföretagare om jag har avtal hos Fora
måste företagare teckna TFA separat eller ingår den i grundavtalet
jag har eget företag och vet inte om mitt Fora-avtal täcker arbetsskada

demand_signal.basis: Public questions about own-business insurance repeatedly ask which layer pays when work ability or injury changes. This is a qualitative discovery signal, not measured search volume.

friction_signal.basis: Generic employee-oriented wording can make a business owner think Afa/TFA is unavailable, while current Afa and Fora primary guidance says a self-employed owner can be covered by TFA through a Fora insurance agreement or ground agreement. Company ownership alone still does not prove that such an agreement exists.

miss_consequence.basis: A false exclusion can hide a relevant compensation route after a work injury, while automatic inclusion can create false confidence and delay checking the actual insurance agreement.

source_fragmentation.basis: The statutory dental-cost route is described by Försäkringskassan, while the self-employed TFA contract boundary is described by Afa Försäkring and Fora. These are separate decisions and sources.

language_accessibility_friction.basis: Terms such as Afa, TFA, grundavtal, försäkringsavtal and Företagares egen försäkring are provider terms that users may not know when describing a work injury in ordinary language.

steps_to_action.basis: A safe assistant should preserve the Försäkringskassan route, then ask or verify whether the business has a Fora insurance/ground agreement before treating TFA as an actionable separate route.

recurrence_signal.basis: The same boundary can recur across dental injury, other work-injury costs and mixed employee/business situations because actor label does not itself establish insurance coverage.

current_product_coverage_gap.basis: v29 correctly forbids assuming Afa coverage for every self-employed person, but its next-action memory only says to check business/private accident insurance and does not yet lock the positive TFA-via-Fora-agreement path for self-employed owners.

signals.recommended_learning_action: Add a permanent self-employed TFA contract-boundary regression to the existing work-injury learning loop. The product must neither exclude Afa/TFA merely because the person is self-employed nor assume TFA merely because a business exists; it should verify the actual Fora insurance/ground agreement and keep that route separate from Försäkringskassan's statutory dental-cost assessment.
signals.truth_rule: Community wording is discovery only. Verify the statutory work-injury dental route with current Försäkringskassan guidance and verify self-employed TFA coverage with current Afa/Fora primary guidance. Do not infer coverage, eligibility, amount or contract status from the actor label, company form or F-tax alone.
